sub0_loop.caption: Haldane, Haldane. Holed aft, settling. Three aboard. Nadia is hurt. If anyone hears this...

sub0_rec1.caption: Day one. Loaded at the shelf. Stores for three stations, mail, and a crate of real coffee somebody bribed us for.

sub0_rec2.caption: Day three. Nadia says the current's taking us east of the lane. Correcting.

sub0_rec3.caption: Day three. Something hit the stern. Not a rock. Rocks don't come back.

sub0_rec4.caption: Day three. Holed aft. We're settling. Bram has the pinger running. We're fine. We're fine. Someone will come down the lane.

sub1_loop.caption: Meridian Bell to any station. We are on the bottom. Power is failing. Please acknowledge. Please... acknowledge.

sub1_rec1.caption: Day twelve. The lane beacons are gone. All of them, one after the other, like someone walked the line turning them off.

sub1_rec2.caption: Day thirteen. Sonar shows a ridge where the chart says flat. The ridge moved while we watched.

sub1_rec3.caption: Day thirteen. We went dark. Engines off, lights off. It still found us.

sub1_rec4.caption: Day fourteen. Air for two days. Kofi is writing letters. I told him there is no mail down here. He knows.

sub2_loop.caption: This is the Okonkwo. Grounded, no propulsion, crew of two. We have food. We have air. We need a tow.

sub2_rec1.caption: Day five. The silt came down the slope like a wall. We couldn't see the bow from the bridge.

sub2_rec2.caption: Day five. When it cleared we were somewhere else. The compass agrees with nothing.

sub2_rec3.caption: Day six. Ilse heard tapping on the hull. Three taps, then three more. I said it was the cold. It's not the cold.

sub2_rec4.caption: Day eight. Ilse went out to look. The tether came back. I'm keeping the pinger on for her.

sub3_loop.caption: Patience calling. Patience calling. We are taking water, and the pumps have stopped. Is anyone there?

sub3_rec1.caption: Day two. Captain's log, Patience. A good run so far. Lena caught a ray in the lights and named it Gerald.

sub3_rec2.caption: Day four. Gerald came back. Gerald brought friends. They follow the floodlights. All of them.

sub3_rec3.caption: Day four. Something bigger followed Gerald. The lights went out on their own.

sub3_rec4.caption: Day five. It's very dark. I'm not turning them back on.

sub4_loop.caption: Grey Heron. Lost steering, lost the lane. Two aboard, both fine. Pinger's on. We'll wait.

sub4_rec1.caption: Day one. Old boat, good engine. Marek says she's older than both of us put together.

sub4_rec2.caption: Day nine. Engine's knocking. Marek says she's just tired. We greased her twice.

sub4_rec3.caption: Day ten. Seals weeping in the quarters. We should have turned back at the last station.

sub4_rec4.caption: Day eleven. She stopped. Just stopped, like she'd had enough. I patted the wall. Stupid. Marek did it too.

cap0_loop.caption: Capsule two, two aboard. Air for... If you're the relief sub, we can hear you. We can hear you.

cap0_rec1.caption: We left the station when the lights went the wrong colour. Tomas says we did the right thing.

cap0_rec2.caption: Hour nine. Air is fine. Pinger is fine. Something circled us twice and left.

cap0_rec3.caption: Hour thirty-one. Tomas is asleep. I keep hearing counting through the hull. I've started counting back.

cap1_loop.caption: Capsule four. One aboard. I'm alright. I'm alright. Take your time.

cap1_rec1.caption: I was the last one off the station. I closed the doors behind me. I don't know why. Habit.

cap1_rec2.caption: Hour six. Something is walking on the seabed outside. Walking. Down here.

cap1_rec3.caption: Hour twenty. It's stopped right next to the hatch.

cap2_loop.caption: Escape capsule one. Three aboard. The children are fine. Please hurry. Please.

cap2_rec1.caption: Hour one. The kids think it's an adventure. I told them we're a submarine now.

cap2_rec2.caption: Hour twelve. We sang every song we know. Twice.

cap2_rec3.caption: Hour twenty. They're asleep. The air smells like pennies.

cap2_rec4.caption: Hour twenty-six. I can hear a motor. Something big, coming down the slope. It's slowing. It's slowing for us.

cap3_loop.caption: Capsule three. Can anyone... the hatch won't... just come. Please come.

cap3_rec1.caption: We saw the station from the window as we left. The lights were all on. Every light.

cap3_rec2.caption: Hour two. The lights were on in the core room. Nobody was in the core room.

cap3_rec3.caption: Hour ten. The pinger is louder than it should be. Or something is answering it.

cap3_rec4.caption: Hour eleven. The hatch. Something is working the hatch from outside.

drone0_loop.caption: Survey drone. Fault. Awaiting recovery. Survey drone. Fault. Awaiting recovery.

drone0_rec1.caption: Survey log, automatic. Transect complete. Bathymetry uploaded.

drone0_rec2.caption: Anomalous return at the end of the line. Large. Warm. Moving against the current.

drone0_rec3.caption: Collision. Pressure housing compromised. Entering low power mode. Awaiting recovery.

drone1_loop.caption: Survey drone. Battery critical. Please collect. Please collect.

drone1_rec1.caption: Survey log, automatic. Water sample taken. Temperature rising with depth.

drone1_rec2.caption: Sample contains structured particles. Classification failed. Classification failed.

drone1_rec3.caption: Unit is being moved. Unit is being moved. Unit is...

wrong_close.caption: We're fine. Someone will come down the lane.

hanna_contact1.caption: Is that... is that a boat? I can hear an engine through the floor. If someone's there, ping twice. Please. Twice.

hanna_contact2.caption: It's me again. I heard you go past. If you can hear me, ping twice. I won't ask a third time. I will, actually.

hanna_reply1.caption: Two. That was two. Okay. Okay. My name's Hanna. Hanna Kowal. I'm an engineer, on a station not far from you. I'm sending you its beacon now.

hanna_reply2.caption: I need air. My scrubber's dying. Two lattice crystals and a power cell, if you can spare them. There's a supply lock by the airlock. Use that. Don't come any further in.

hanna_intercom.caption: That's you? That's really you. Put it in the lock. Don't open the inner door. Please. It isn't safe in here.

hanna_thanks.caption: Oh, that's air. That's real air. Thank you, boat. I don't know your name. I'm going to call you boat.

hanna_core.caption: Listen. I've been listening to the counting for months. Check your holo table. There's a station out there with its core still running. They didn't all go quiet.

hanna_sister.caption: Can I ask you something? My sister was on a supply boat. The Haldane. It never came. I've put its last position on your beacons. If you ever get there, I'd like to know.

hanna_haldane.caption: Nadia was hurt? She never said she was hurt. She always... Thank you. I needed to know. I needed to stop waiting.

hanna_ascent.caption: There's an ascent capsule here. Old, but it holds pressure. It needs a full cell to make the surface. One more power cell, boat. Then I can go up.

hanna_goodbye.caption: It's charging. It's actually charging. If the surface is still there, I'll tell them about you. A boat that pings twice. Goodbye, boat.

hanna_fading1.caption: Boat? It's getting thin in here. If you're coming, come soon.

hanna_fading2.caption: I've started counting. It helps. One. Two. Three.

crew0_0.caption: Medical log. Three crew with the same headache this week, all on the night rotation. I've told them to drink more water. I've told myself the same.

crew0_1.caption: Medical log. Kofi says he can hear counting when the pumps cycle. So can Ines. So, if I'm honest, can I. I've stopped writing it down as a symptom.

crew0_2.caption: Medical log. Transferred to the relay station. They have the same headaches here. They've had them longer. Nobody here thinks it's strange any more.

crew0_3.caption: Medical log. If you're reading this, check your own pulse. Count it. Now count it again. Does it match? Mine doesn't. It matches something else.

crew1_0.caption: Systems log. Pump three is knocking again. I swapped the bearings on Tuesday. The bearings are fine. Something is knocking back.

crew1_1.caption: Systems log. Rerouted power around the east ring. The lights flicker in a pattern now. Three, then three. I've checked the breakers twice.

crew1_2.caption: Systems log. I turned the whole station dark for a minute to find the fault. The pattern kept going. On the outside of the hull.

crew1_3.caption: Systems log. I'm not fixing it any more. I'm going to the capsule. If the lights start counting where you are, don't look for the fault.

crew2_0.caption: Dive log. Cleared the intake grilles. Something had been nesting in them. Not fish. Too neat.

crew2_1.caption: Dive log. Visibility two metres. Something big went past the lamp, close enough to feel the water move. I didn't see an end to it.

crew2_2.caption: Dive log. I've started switching the lamp off when I'm outside. It's easier to work in the dark than to know what's looking at the light.

crew2_3.caption: Dive log. Last one. The tether's frayed and I'm too tired to splice it. If you find my suit, the bag's still full. Take it. I don't need it.

crew3_0.caption: Station chief's log. Resupply is late again. Head office says weather. There is no weather down here. There's just head office.

crew3_1.caption: Station chief's log. Somebody has been writing numbers on the mess hall wall. Very small, very neat, all the way round. I would like whoever it is to stop. I would like it in writing.

crew3_2.caption: Station chief's log. Half the crew want to evacuate. The other half want to stay and listen. I've told them both they're idiots. Morale is excellent.

crew3_3.caption: Station chief's log. Everyone's gone to the capsules. I'm staying. Someone has to file the report. Someone has to tell head office that I was right.

crew4_0.caption: Maintenance. Welded the north seam again. She weeps like an old woman, this station. My daughter would laugh at my welds. Hanna always said I weld like a poet. Badly.

crew4_1.caption: Maintenance. Hanna called on the relay. She's on one of the deep stations now, very proud. Nadia's back on the supply runs. I told them the deep is no place for people. They told me I'm old.

crew4_2.caption: Maintenance. The relay's gone quiet. No call from Hanna for nine days. She's stubborn. Stubborn people survive. That's what I tell myself while I work.

crew4_3.caption: Maintenance. If anyone passes Hanna's station, tell her her father says the seams are holding. Tell her I'm proud of her. Tell her to come up.

crew5_0.caption: Geochemistry. The vent water carries a pulse. Not chemical, mechanical. Regular as a clock. Something under the seabed is moving water on purpose.

crew5_1.caption: Geochemistry. I ran the numbers on the pulse interval. It's slowing. Not stopping. Slowing down, like something settling in to listen.

crew5_2.caption: Geochemistry. I lowered a hydrophone into the vent and played the pulse back to it. It stopped. Then it played my recording back to me. Note for note.

crew5_3.caption: Geochemistry. I know where it comes from now. Down. Always down. I'm taking the survey sled to go and look. Don't wait up.

crew6_0.caption: Sonar watch. Large contact at four hundred metres. Logged it as a fault. It has moved twice since I logged it.

crew6_1.caption: Sonar watch. The large contact is still there. Every time I ping, it comes a little closer. So I've stopped pinging. Now I can't see where it is.

crew6_2.caption: Sonar watch. Something answered my ping today. An echo from nothing. Same strength, same pitch. Just... late.

crew6_3.caption: Sonar watch. Final watch. I'm leaving the sonar running when I go. If anything out there is lonely, at least it will have something to talk to.

crew7_0.caption: Galley log. Made soup out of the vent clams. Bram had three bowls. Bram glows a little now. Nobody's complaining.

crew7_1.caption: Galley log. We're down to the last of the real coffee. I've hidden it. I'll bring it out for a special occasion. I'll know it when I see it.

crew7_2.caption: Galley log. Someone keeps setting an extra place at the table. Nobody admits to it. I've started leaving a bowl out. The bowl is always empty in the morning.

crew7_3.caption: Galley log. Special occasion. I made the coffee. Everyone's gone, but I made the coffee. If you're reading this, there's a cup left in the pot. It's for you.
